title: Git facts off the request path
summary: Decision-ready architecture for Git facts in Agent Studio, revised from d1e6933f5 on aeb25d97b. The inventory covers card reads, file-root probes, project integration and Wiki history, names adjacent migration exclusions, and recognises the integrated AGT-3086 result-history fix. Recommends a generation-keyed SQLite fact store with one writer per repository: interim on the backend, then a fenced runner-host producer feeding task-server.db. Ref/config generations control invalidation; durable snapshots cover restart and crash recovery. S1 measures and freezes GET exceptions and index/runtime budgets before enforcing the guard. Eight bounded slices target card list and required detail handlers under 200 ms with zero request Git after S3 to S5; excluded route migrations must also finish before claiming zero Git across all GETs. D1 to D8 carry working recommendations. The canonical delivery is docs/git-facts-architecture/ under the concept placement contract.

implementationTasks.title: S1 Guard Git spawns on read requests and enforce budgets as tests
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# S1 Guard Git spawns on read requests and enforce budgets as tests

Source: `docs/git-facts-architecture/index.html`, request families R1 to R13, Inventory boundary, migration S1 and decisions D6/D7. This slice lands first. R-numbers are explanatory groups, not the complete backend route manifest or the guard allowlist.

## Change

1. Route every backend Git process start through one boundary that records `GitProcessTelemetry` and registers children. Audit direct starts, including `TaskFileHistoryService.RunGit` (`backend/Features/Tasks/TaskFileHistoryService.cs:616` at aeb25d97b) and its `ProcessTaskHistoryGitRunner`, `GitService.RollbackGitArgs`, `RemoteReviewPlanBuilder.Git`, `CommitCandidateGate`, `PublishActionService` and `WorkspaceArtifactPushWorker`. Preserve cancellation, argument escaping and budgets. Every ProcessStartInfo must set CreateNoWindow = true.
2. Add an ambient read-request scope from HTTP method and route metadata to every GET endpoint, including the board read gate. Existing service labels such as wiki/*, board/merge-status, board/integration-status, git/commit-presence and publish/derive remain useful but do not replace an outer HTTP scope. Account for inherited scopes and direct spawn bypasses. Add an architecture assertion against unguarded Git starts.
3. Before enabling enforcement, enumerate registered GET routes and exercise their real call chains on isolated fixtures with cold/warm caches, a moved ref, missing files, checkout/fixed-SHA Wiki modes and history variants. Record route template, method, scenario, spawn count/commands, owner and removal slice. Include R4 to R8, R11 (files and checkout, live/at/history), R12 (/api/git/integration), R13 (Wiki), and the project Git, repository-document and publishing families named under Inventory boundary. Do not copy an assumed R4-to-R8 allowlist. R6 is already Git-free after AGT-3086; include it only if a reproduced regression exists. R9/R10 are writes and are not read-guard exceptions.
4. Commit the measured initial violator manifest and its reviewed digest in S1. Freeze exact method/route/scenario entries and per-scenario spawn ceilings. With that baseline loaded, a non-exempt read spawn throws GitProcessOnReadRequestException in tests and Debug. Production counts/logs it and raises a health warning without throwing. Baseline exceptions continue to count as visible migration debt, without permanent warnings for their expected traffic; an exceeded ceiling or new route warns and fails a test. Tests reject growth of the frozen manifest; later slices can only remove entries or lower ceilings. Never generate or expand exceptions automatically in production or during a normal test run. Unexercised routes are coverage gaps, not wildcard exceptions; S1 must close the GET census before acceptance.
5. Add a fixture with 3,000 cards, at least 2,000 archived, 200 or more in review, duplicate ids, packed refs and a worktree. Include escalated cards, existing and absent orchestrator-follow-up.md, decision.html and decision.json, result/file histories, and code/workspace source variants. Use injected TimeProvider for TTL, ref-event and guard tests; no new wall-clock reads or unmarked fixed dates in test files.

## Budget tests

- GET /api/tasks/ and /grouped: 0 Git spawns; serialized summary size at most 2 KiB per card. Core and details resources: 0 Git spawns.
- Measure 30 unchanged-input GitStateIndexService runs after warm-up on the 3,000-card fixture, recording p50/p95 duration and spawns. Freeze the numeric runtime ceiling at measured p95 plus 10 percent, capped at the current 90 s run deadline, in the benchmark manifest; do not accept a timeout or a partial projection as a passing run. Subsequent runs must remain below that ceiling. S2 tightens unchanged-input p95 to 2 s with 0 spawns. Record first-build and changed-ref durations separately.
- Deterministic tests enforce spawn ceilings, payload bytes, complete per-card results, duplicate isolation and the index deadline using injected time. Actual elapsed-time/performance checks run separately with Category=MachineBound on a documented reference host; they must also pass before S1 delivery. Do not substitute fake elapsed time for a measured p95.
- Record a 30-switch baseline per required card request (p50, p95, spawns), including R11 file reads on escalation/decision opens. Keep the route census, frozen index budget and measurements in the card results.

Do not change caching or the producer in this slice. Existing known debt is grandfathered only through the measured manifest. Performance targets not yet achieved are recorded for their owning slice rather than falsely claimed as passing in S1.

acceptanceScope.slice: S1 Guard Git spawns on read requests and enforce budgets as tests
criteria: Every backend Git process start uses the telemetry/child-registry boundary; architecture coverage detects bypasses.

The initial exact GET violator manifest is measured across the registered endpoint census, including file, integration, Wiki and explicitly excluded migration families, with no wildcard entries; R9/R10 writes are excluded.
After the baseline is frozen, a non-exempt read spawn throws in Debug/tests and warns in production. Known debt is counted; exceeded ceilings fail tests and warn; manifest growth fails a test.
List, grouped, core and details have 0 request spawns on the 3,000-card duplicate-id fixture; list summaries stay at most 2 KiB per card.

A measured 30-run unchanged-input index p95 budget (baseline plus 10 percent, at most 90 s) is frozen and enforced, with complete results; deterministic deadline tests use injected time and elapsed-time checks carry MachineBound.
A 30-switch baseline includes escalated card file reads, missing decision files, p50/p95 and per-route spawn counts, and is preserved with the route census.

implementationTasks.title: S2 Persist Git fact generations and restore them on start
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# S2 Persist Git fact generations and restore them on start

Source: `docs/git-facts-architecture/index.html`, section 03 (the fact store, writers, invalidation, cold start and crash recovery) and section 04 (S2); decisions D1, D3 and D7. Depends on S1.

## Change

1. Add the Git fact store as SQLite `git-facts.db` in the backend state directory with the tables `git_repositories`, `git_ref_generations`, `card_git_facts` and `fact_producer_health`, exactly as the Dossier specifies. Keep the schema in one place so S7 can create the same tables in `task-server/TaskServerStore.cs`.
2. Make `GitStateIndexService` the only writer. Publish each repository generation (ref object IDs, ref fingerprint, `config_generation`, settings version, producer epoch, card rows) in one transaction in WAL mode, then swap the in-memory pointer that `TaskListGitProjectionCache` reads. Reject a publish whose producer epoch is lower than the stored one.
3. On start, load the last generation per repository and serve it with state `restored` and its age. Compute `ReadOnlyGitRefFingerprint` and the configuration signature from files. If both match, mark it `ready` without starting Git. Otherwise run a normal delta run.
4. Advance `config_generation` only from the existing watcher events for `config`, `config.worktree` and included files (`GitStateIndexService.cs:309-325`). Do not spawn `git config --list` at the start of every run (`:477`). A task event must not start Git when no card's input signature changed.
5. Run `PRAGMA quick_check` on open. On failure, move the file aside, raise a typed health event and rebuild within the spawn budget, answering `warming` per card.
6. Replace the repository-wide abort after `min(3, n)` card failures (`TaskListGitProjectionCache.cs:392-393`) with a repository health state that keeps the last good generation.

Do not change what is computed per card in this slice; S3 does that.

The 3,000-card unchanged-input index benchmark introduced in S1 must now have p95 at most 2 s and 0 Git spawns. Reuse the same fixture and documented reference host. Deadline and configuration-event tests inject the clock; measured runtime checks carry Category=MachineBound.

acceptanceScope.slice: S2 Persist Git fact generations and restore them on start
criteria: Restart with unchanged refs serves restored Git facts before any Git process and reaches ready with 0 spawns.
A task event that changes no card input signature starts 0 Git processes.
Killing the process during a run leaves the previous generation current and readable.
A publish with an older producer epoch is rejected in a test.
A corrupt store file is detected on start and rebuilt without request-time Git.
On the S1 reference host, unchanged-input index p95 is at most 2 s for 3,000 cards, with 0 spawns and complete per-card results.

implementationTasks.title: S3 Serve card Git facts and the default diff from the store
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# S3 Serve card Git facts and the default diff from the store

Source: `docs/git-facts-architecture/index.html`, section 03 (invalidation by ref generation, reads) and section 04 (S3). Depends on S2. Diff object keys follow `docs/studio-route-ownership/index.html` D1.

## Change

1. Add `git_commit_facts` (parents, tree, author time, subject, trailers, name-status and numstat per path), keyed by repository and SHA, immutable. The producer fills it for new SHAs in one batched read per run, for example `git log --no-walk --name-status --numstat` or `cat-file --batch`.
2. Add `git_reachability` per target ref. On a fast-forward from `old` to `new`, append `rev-list old..new`. On a non-fast-forward move, recompute that ref once. Classify all cards by an in-memory join. Enable `core.commitGraph` and `fetch.writeCommitGraph` on managed checkouts.
3. Take a card's attributed SHAs from `task.json` and `result_handoffs` as its input signature. Stop `log --all --grep` (`GitService.cs:6965`) on read paths, and move the attribution backfill out of the `/commits` GET (`TaskGitEndpoints.cs:418`) into the producer.
4. Serve these from the store with generation, age and ETag, and with 0 Git spawns:
   - `/provenance` (replaces the per-commit `merge-base` calls in `TaskProvenanceService.cs:358-366`)
   - `/commits`, `/commits/files` and `/commit`
   - `/commits/{sha}/files`
   - `/runs/{i}/commits` and `/runs/{i}/files`
5. At publication, the producer writes a SHA-keyed diff object for each attributed commit and for the aggregate. The default diff that `git-pane.service.ts:331-343` selects is served from that object. A missing object answers `warming` and queues a priority computation.
6. Publish the project integration view R12 from the same ref/config generation. `GET /api/git/integration` (`backend/Host/SystemEndpoints.cs:156`) must not call live `ProjectIntegrationViewService.Build` (`backend/Features/Git/ProjectIntegrationViewService.cs:190-214` at aeb25d97b). Move the two ancestor walks, publisher merge log and nested BuildLookup to the producer, share reachability with card classification, and persist the queue/publisher/promotion projection in git_project_views keyed by ref/config plus task-index generation. Task-only changes may rejoin stored facts but must not trigger Git. Serve last good or warming on a miss, with generation and ETag, never inline recomputation.
7. Remove all migrated exact route entries from the S1 manifest, including R12. Retain only measured exceptions still owned by later or explicitly excluded migration work. The S3 pass alone does not establish the card-detail target; S4 covers file reads and S5 removes request-time scans.

acceptanceScope.slice: S3 Serve card Git facts and the default diff from the store
criteria: Provenance, commits, commits/files, commit and the default diff spawn 0 Git processes on the request thread.
Each of those routes has p95 under 200 ms on the 3,000-card fixture over a 30-switch replay.
A single fast-forward of the target ref is reflected in all card facts within 2 s on the fixture.
A non-fast-forward move removes containment and is covered by a test.
The S1 allowlist no longer contains R4, R5 or the run file routes.
GET /api/git/integration has 0 request spawns, p95 under 200 ms on the fixture, and no history walk or live BuildLookup on a cold projection miss; its S1 exception is removed.

implementationTasks.title: S4 Serve card files and result history without request Git
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# S4 Serve card files and result history without request Git

Source: `docs/git-facts-architecture/index.html`, R6 and R11, Reads and migration S4; decision D4. Depends on S1 only. Reuse AGT-3086 on aeb25d97b: ResultHistoryQueryService already reads persisted legacy snapshots and LegacyResultHistoryBackfill owns the background walk. Do not recreate that fix or reintroduce its removed fallback. Coordinate code/checkout ownership with AGT-3017.

## Change

1. Add the result_versions index (task key, version id, producer, lane, run index, verdict, steps, timestamp, content hash, source commit) to the shared Git fact store schema. ResultVersionStore indexes each status snapshot at write time; reuse the existing legacy backfill and its progress/resume data to import rows. If S2 has not landed, introduce only the common schema/bootstrap needed for these tables, with ResultVersionStore and the backfill as their writers. S2 must reuse this bootstrap. Keep snapshot content in its existing location.
2. Keep ResultHistoryQueryService.List/Read on persisted facts and bounded content reads. Preserve pending/failed legacy state and prohibit calls to GetWorkspaceResultHistory from any read handler. An unimported historical version reports warming, never a synchronous walk.
3. Remove Git-root discovery from live card file reads. At aeb25d97b, TaskFilesEndpoints.cs:54-101 calls ReadFile/GetHistory; TaskFileHistoryService.ResolveCandidates builds workspace/code candidates (:313-386), each calling ResolveGitRoot (:543-545). Split live path resolution from Git history resolution. A live GET /api/tasks/{id}/files/{path} must read the authorised file or return its existing not-found response without any rev-parse, even on cold start, an absent file or automatic source fallback. Apply the same rule to /checkout/{path}. Preserve path containment, workspace-before-code precedence, source headers, extension handling and authorization.
4. Store repository-root identity for historical work in a producer-owned mapping keyed by configured repository/workspace identity and config generation, invalidated by checkout/worktree relocation. History workers may resolve roots; requests may not. Persist git_path_histories entries and git_file_objects SHA/path content references from bounded background jobs, serialized through the single repository fact producer. Reuse git_repositories for root mappings; if S2 is not present, introduce its minimal shared bootstrap and writer interface, which S2 then extends. /files/{path}/history, /checkout/{path}/history and both at= revision variants read those facts, or answer warming and queue work on a miss. No request caller may reach GetHistory's live log walk or direct git show. Use a separate path-history/object index; do not overload result_versions with arbitrary source files.
5. Remove the exact R6/R11 entries, if present, from the measured S1 manifest. Add route regressions for orchestrator-follow-up.md and results/decision.html/json as read by escalation-summary.component.ts:128 and decision-surface.component.ts:122-127, plus pipeline-step/files-pane arbitrary file reads. Include missing files, source variants, historical reads, packed refs and worktrees.

Use injected clocks for deadline/refresh tests and CreateNoWindow = true for every process fixture. Put real latency checks in Category=MachineBound. Do not rewrite existing mixed line endings.

acceptanceScope.slice: S4 Serve card files and result history without request Git
criteria: GET result-history and result-history/{versionId} keep 0 Git spawns; result-history p95 is under 50 ms on the fixture, using the existing resumable AGT-3086 backfill.
All R11 files/checkout live, history and at= variants have 0 request Git spawns and p95 under 200 ms over 30 switches at current board size and on the 3,000-card fixture.

Cold or missing orchestrator-follow-up.md, decision.html and decision.json reads perform no Git-root discovery; source precedence, path containment, authorization and existing not-found behavior are preserved.
Historical data misses report warming and queue budgeted background work; no file read can execute ResolveGitRoot, log or show on the request thread.
New status versions are indexed at write time; backfill remains resumable and reports its pending/failed state; migrated R6/R11 exceptions are absent from the S1 manifest.

implementationTasks.title: S5 Remove request-time scans from the board and persist the slim board
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# S5 Remove request-time scans from the board and persist the slim board

Source: `docs/git-facts-architecture/index.html`, section 01 (R1, R3), section 03 (cold start) and section 04 (S5). Depends on S1. Coordinate with `docs/task-switch-performance/index.html` card 5 ("Reuse board records across task navigation").

## Change

1. In `TaskIndexCache.EnsureFresh` (`backend/Features/Tasks/TaskIndexCache.cs:408-480`), stop letting a request become the refresher (`:446-451`). A request reads the current snapshot and signals the background refresher. Mutation paths that need read-your-write keep the existing published-generation wait, bounded at 2 s.
2. Persist the last published slim board summaries (`BoardCardSummary`) per project, with their index generation. On start, serve them as `restored` while the first background scan runs, instead of blocking on it (`:454-457`).
3. Remove the `ScanAllJobs` call from the legacy detail route (`TaskCrudEndpoints.cs:404`); use the reference index snapshot.
4. Keep the AGT-2703 ETag contract and the single-flight memo in `BoardReadConcurrencyGate`; add the persisted generation to the signature.

## Combined card-detail acceptance

S5's local board/scan work still depends only on S1. After S3, S4 and S5 land, run their combined 30-switch replay at the current board size (235 live plus 2,088 archived) and at 3,000 cards. Include escalated cards, existing/absent follow-up and decision files, default diffs and result histories. Every required detail handler must have p95 under 200 ms and 0 request Git; board list/grouped have the same budget. Record time to receive all required detail responses separately without claiming that the per-handler budget proves browser-render time. The combined card-detail claim is gated on all three slices, not S3 plus S4 alone. Wiki/publishing and other explicitly excluded project routes remain measured debt under their named owners, not evidence that the entire GET manifest is empty.

acceptanceScope.slice: S5 Remove request-time scans from the board and persist the slim board
criteria: No board, core or detail request runs TaskIndexCache.Refresh on its own thread; a test asserts it.
GET /api/tasks/ and /grouped have p95 under 200 ms at the current board size and on the 3,000-card fixture.
The first board read after process start answers within 2 s from the persisted board, marked restored.
ETag and 304 behaviour is unchanged for unchanged inputs.

After S3/S4/S5 are all present, a combined 30-switch replay including escalated cards and missing decision files proves each required detail handler p95 under 200 ms with 0 request Git at current size and on the 3,000-card fixture; aggregate response completion time is also reported.

implementationTasks.title: S6 Take Git out of mutation handlers and review replanning
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# S6 Take Git out of mutation handlers and review replanning

Source: `docs/git-facts-architecture/index.html`, section 01 (R9, R10), section 03 (mutations and review planning) and section 04 (S6); decision D5. Depends on S2.

## Change

1. Add a producer request: "publish a generation at least as new as ref fingerprint X". The producer deduplicates requests and serves them ahead of sweeps.
2. Replace direct `TaskIntegrationStatusService.BuildLookup` calls on request threads with that request plus a store read, bounded at 2 s:
   - `TaskTransitionService.cs:316` inside `MoveAsync`, and the other transition call sites at `:1688`, `:1707`, `:1740` and `:1816`
   - `TaskIntegrationRecoveryEndpoints.cs:40`
   If the bound is reached, return 409 `integration-check-pending` with a retry hint. The Studio retries once and shows the pending state.
3. Queue project-settings-triggered replanning (`ProjectSettingsEndpoints.cs:1415-1442`) to `ReviewInfrastructureRetryScheduler` instead of running per attempt inside the request.
4. Keep the authoritative acceptance checks exactly as strict as today. A display cache never bypasses them; the check reads a generation proven current for the ref fingerprint.

acceptanceScope.slice: S6 Take Git out of mutation handlers and review replanning
criteria: A completion move and a project settings write start 0 Git processes on the request thread.
Completion move p95 stays under 2.2 s including the producer wait; timeouts return a typed 409.
Queued review attempts are replanned in the background with the same plans as before, proven by a test.
Acceptance outcomes on the existing acceptance test suite are unchanged.

implementationTasks.title: S7 Publish Git fact generations from the runner host
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# S7 Publish Git fact generations from the runner host

Source: `docs/git-facts-architecture/index.html`, sections 02 (option C), 03 (writers, epoch) and 04 (S7); decision D1. Depends on S3 and on AGT-2737 B6 readiness. Extends, and does not repeat, the cards "Git object contract and Task Server store" and "Runner publication of Git facts and diff objects" in `docs/studio-route-ownership/index.html`, which own diff objects.

## Change

1. Create the S2 and S3 tables, plus the S4 root mappings and file-history/object indexes before their remote cutover, in `task-server/TaskServerStore.cs` with the same schema, inside `InWriteTransactionAsync`, and include them in `FullBackupService`.
2. On the runner host, beside the canonical checkout (ADR-0073), run one fact producer per repository under a Task Server lease with a monotonic epoch. Publish generations as a new outbox kind `runner.git-generation`. The payload carries repository id, ref object IDs, config generation, new commit facts, reachability delta, card rows, epoch and checksum, and its ingestion is idempotent. Give the existing `runner.git-facts` event (`runner/DurableHandoffPayloads.cs:28-34`) a reader, or fold it in.
3. The Task Server validates epoch and monotonic generation and stores atomically. Readers in the Studio go through the Task Server projection.
4. Run in shadow for one repository: both producers publish, and a comparer reports mismatched card facts. Then cut over per repository, and stop the backend producer for that repository.

acceptanceScope.slice: S7 Publish Git fact generations from the runner host
criteria: Task Server ingestion rejects an older epoch and a non-monotonic generation in tests.
One week of shadow run reports zero mismatched card facts for the pilot repository.
After cutover, the task server host starts 0 Git processes for facts of that repository.
Board and card reads keep their S3 to S5 budgets through the Task Server.

implementationTasks.title: S8 Benchmark Git readers and repository maintenance
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# S8 Benchmark Git readers and repository maintenance

Source: `docs/git-facts-architecture/index.html`, section 02 (option D) and section 04 (S8); decision D8. Depends on S3.

## Change

Benchmark these readers for the producer's operations: resolve refs, merge-base and reachability delta, name-status and numstat for a SHA, effective config, and a single file patch.

- the bounded CLI
- one long-lived `git cat-file --batch` and `--batch-check` reader
- LibGit2Sharp
- a small gitoxide sidecar

Use identical fixtures on Windows and Linux: packed refs, worktrees, conditional includes, shallow history, missing objects, concurrent ref movement and the 3,000-card fixture. Measure cold and warm, process start, total CPU, memory, p50 and p95, and correctness against CLI output. Measure the effect of these maintenance settings on the same fixture:

- `core.commitGraph`
- `fetch.writeCommitGraph`
- scheduled `git maintenance`
- `core.fsmonitor` with `core.untrackedCache`, only where status is still needed

Record the decision in the Dossier implementation log. Adopt a library only with a CPU reduction of 30 percent or more and full parity.

acceptanceScope.slice: S8 Benchmark Git readers and repository maintenance
criteria: A benchmark report with p50, p95, CPU and correctness per reader and operation on Windows and Linux is in the card results.
Maintenance settings are measured on the same fixture and the chosen settings are applied to managed checkouts.
The adoption decision is recorded with the 30 percent CPU and parity rule applied.
